Profile.guidance: Indicate a score from 1 to 5. Decimals can be used

Profile.question: Target maturity level process domain
Profile.guidance: Indicate a score from 1 to 5. Decimals can be used

Profile.guidance: Indicate a score from 1 to 5. Decimals can be used

SOC Tooling (Technology domain).question: SIEM / UEBA
SOC Tooling (Technology domain).guidance: Security Information and Event management tooling. Used to gather logging information from company assets and correlate events. Also includes User and Entity Behaviour Analytics (UEBA)

SOC Tooling (Technology domain).question: NDR
SOC Tooling (Technology domain).guidance: Network security solution, used detect network exploits and anomalous network activity and perform network forensics

SOC Tooling (Technology domain).question: EDR
SOC Tooling (Technology domain).guidance: End-point security solution, used to prevent, detect and respond to threats on end-points

SOC Tooling (Technology domain).question: SOAR
SOC Tooling (Technology domain).guidance: Used to automate workflows and SOC actions, support incident response and orchestrate between different security products

SOC Services (services domain).question: Security Monitoring
SOC Services (services domain).guidance: The security monitoring service aims at detecting security incidents and events

SOC Services (services domain).question: Security Incident Management
SOC Services (services domain).guidance: The security incident management service aims at responding to security incidents in a timely, accurate and organized fashion

SOC Services (services domain).question: Security Analysis
SOC Services (services domain).guidance: The security analysis service supports security monitoring and security incident management. Analysis includes event analysis and forensic analysis

SOC Services (services domain).question: Threat Intelligence
SOC Services (services domain).guidance: The threat intelligence service provides information about potential threats that can be used in security monitoring, security incident response, security analysis and threat hunting

SOC Services (services domain).question: Threat Hunting
SOC Services (services domain).guidance: The hunting service takes a proactive approach to finding threats in the infrastructure. Threat intelligence is often used to guide hunting efforts

SOC Services (services domain).question: Vulnerability Management
SOC Services (services domain).guidance: The vulnerability management service is used to detect vulnerabilities in assets by discovery and actively scanning assets for known vulnerabilities

SOC Services (services domain).question: Log Management
SOC Services (services domain).guidance: The log management service is used to collect, store and retain logging. Can be used for compliance purposes as well as investigation purposes

Business Drivers.question: Have you identified the main business drivers?
Business Drivers.guidance: Example business drivers: cyber crime prevention, risk reduction, law / regulation, audit / compliance, business continuity

Business Drivers.question: Have you documented the main business drivers?
Business Drivers.guidance: Documentation of business drivers is important for demonstrable business alignment

Business Drivers.question: Do you use business drivers in the decision making process?
Business Drivers.guidance: e.g. to determine priorities or make decisions regarding the on-boarding of new services or operations

Business Drivers.question: Do you regularly check if the current service catalogue is aligned with business drivers?
Business Drivers.guidance: i.e. do you check for services or operations that outside the scope of business drivers?

Business Drivers.question: Have the business drivers been validated with business stakeholders?
Business Drivers.guidance: Business stakeholders can be C-level management

Customers.question: Have you identified the SOC customers?
Customers.guidance: Types of customers, customer requirements / expectations, etc.

Customers.question: Please specify your customers:
Customers.guidance: Use this as a guideline for answering 2.1. This is also potentially useful for insights and comparison with previous assessments.

Customers.question: Have you documented the main SOC customers?
Customers.guidance: Formal registration of customer contact details, place in the organization, geolocation, etc.

Customers.question: Do you differentiate output towards these specific customers?
Customers.guidance: For example, are communication style and contents to Business customers different than that to IT?

Customers.question: Do you have service level agreements with these customers?
Customers.guidance: Service level agreements are used to provide standardized services operating within known boundaries

Customers.question: Do you regularly send updates to your customers?
Customers.guidance: For example: changes in service scope or delivery. Can also be reports, dashboards, etc.

Customers.question: Do you actively measure and manage customer satisfaction?
Customers.guidance: Understanding customer satisfaction will help to better align with business needs

Charter.question: Does the SOC have a formal charter document in place?
Please specify elements of the charter document:
Is the SOC charter document regularly updated?
Charter.guidance: Regularity should be matched to your own internal policy. At least yearly is recommended

Charter.question: Is the SOC charter document approved by the business / CISO?
Charter.guidance: Approval from the relevant stakeholders will aid in business support for SOC operations

Charter.question: Are all stakeholders familiar with the SOC charter document contents?
Charter.guidance: Making stakeholders aware of the contents helps in getting organizational support for security operations

Governance.question: Does the SOC have a governance process in place?
Governance.guidance: A governance process is required to determine the way the SOC should be managed

Governance.question: Have all governance elements been identified?
Governance.guidance: Possible governance elements can be found in under 4.3

Governance.question: Is cost management in place?
Governance.guidance: Managing costs is required to justify budget allocation for the SOC and ensure continued service delivery in the future

Governance.question: Are all governance elements formally documented?
Governance.guidance: Formal documentation should be signed off and stored in a quality management system

Governance.question: Are SOC governance meetings regularly held?
Governance.guidance: Meetings at different levels (operational, tactical, strategic) should be formalised in Terms of Reference (ToR) and driven by metrics

Governance.question: Is the governance process regularly reviewed?
Governance.guidance: Frequency should be matched to your own internal policy. At least yearly is recommended

Governance.question: Is the governance process aligned with all stakeholders?
Governance.guidance: Alignment will help the SOC obtain required mandate, budget and management support

Governance.question: Is the SOC regularly audited or subjected to (external) assessments?
Governance.guidance: Frequency should be matched to the SOC policy. At least yearly is recommended. 3rd party assessments have a higher objectivity

Governance.question: Is there an active cooperation with other SOCs (external)?
Governance.guidance: Exchange of best practices, intelligence and actions on threats with other SOCs is vital for improving cyber defence

Privacy & Policy.question: Is there an information security policy in place that supports the SOC activities?
Privacy & Policy.guidance: A clear security policy that supports SOC operations provides guidance and helps to enforce mandate for the SOC in the organisation

Privacy & Policy.question: Has a SOC policy been created?
Privacy & Policy.guidance: A SOC policy is to outline the rules to which SOC personnel and SOC management needs to adhere

Privacy & Policy.question: Please specify elements of the SOC policy
Is the SOC consulted in the creation and updates of operational security policy?
Privacy & Policy.guidance: Consulting the SOC in the creation of security policy will ensure that SOC activities are properly mentioned and enforceable

Privacy & Policy.question: Is a reporting policy for security incidents in place?
Privacy & Policy.guidance: A reporting policy for security incidents will aid the SOC in identifying incidents and threats in the organization

Privacy & Policy.question: Is a privacy policy regarding security monitoring of employees in place?
Privacy & Policy.guidance: A privacy policy should state that monitoring of employees is possible within acceptable limits

Privacy & Policy.question: Does the SOC operate in compliance with all applicable privacy laws and regulations?
Privacy & Policy.guidance: Local laws and regulations as well as company policy may apply and should all be considered

Privacy & Policy.question: Does the SOC cooperate with legal departments regarding privacy matters?
Privacy & Policy.guidance: Cooperation will ensure that the SOC is enabled to perform activities, rather than blocked

Privacy & Policy.question: Are specific procedures in place for dealing with privacy related investigations?
Privacy & Policy.guidance: Privacy related issues require careful examination, especially those potentially leading to court cases

Privacy & Policy.question: Is the SOC aware of all information that it processes and is subject to privacy regulations?
Privacy & Policy.guidance: Such information includes IP addresses, customer identifiers, user names, host names (for personally owned devices), etc.

Privacy & Policy.question: Is a Privacy Impact Assessment (PIA) regularly conducted?
Privacy & Policy.guidance: Can be used to determine the impact of monitoring on privacy, and can help uncover potential violations

Employees.question: How many FTE’s are in your SOC?
Employees.guidance: Include both internal and external FTE's

Employees.question: Do you use external employees / contractors in your SOC?
Employees.guidance: External employees can be hired experts to fill in vacant positions or perform project activities

Employees.question: If yes, specify the number of external FTE's
Does the current size of the SOC meet FTE requirements?
Employees.guidance: i.e. is the SOC size sufficient to realize business goals?

Employees.question: Does the SOC meet requirements for internal to external employee FTE ratio?
Employees.guidance: Note: requirements do not need to be explicit. Set importance to 'None' if you have no external employees.

Employees.question: Does the SOC meet requirements for internal to external employee skillset?
Employees.guidance: i.e. Are there any crucial skills amongst external employees? Set importance to 'None' if you have no external employees

Employees.question: Are all positions filled?
Employees.guidance: Unfilled positions may be due to deficiencies in the recruitment process

Employees.question: Do you have a recruitment process in place?
Employees.guidance: A recruitment process is required to obtain new employees in a market where talent is scarce

Employees.question: Do you have a talent acquisition process in place?
Employees.guidance: Talent recruitment can be vital for SOC success, but talent retaining is equally important

Employees.question: Do you have specific KSAOs established for SOC personnel?
Employees.guidance: Knowledge, Skills, Abilities and Other attributes (KSAOs) should be in place: technical, cognitive, social and character

Employees.question: Do you actively seek to create a psychologically safe environment for SOC personnel?
Employees.guidance: A psychologically safe environment is an environment where everyone is able to speak their mind and feel valued

Roles and Hierarchy.question: Do you formally differentiate roles within the SOC?
Roles and Hierarchy.guidance: Use the roles in 2.2 to determine if you have all roles required in the SOC

Roles and Hierarchy.question: Which of the following roles are present in your SOC?
Do you differentiate tiers within these roles?
Roles and Hierarchy.guidance: If you have no tiers, and you feel this is not a restriction, select importance 'None'

Roles and Hierarchy.question: Are all roles sufficiently staffed?
Roles and Hierarchy.guidance: Consider the staffing levels (desired FTE count) as well as knowledge and experience for all roles

Roles and Hierarchy.question: Is there a role-based hierarchy in your SOC?
Roles and Hierarchy.guidance: If you have no hierarchy, and you feel this is not a restriction, select importance 'None'

Roles and Hierarchy.question: Have you formally documented all SOC roles?
Roles and Hierarchy.guidance: Possible documentation elements can be found in under 2.7

Roles and Hierarchy.question: Please specify elements in the role documentation:
Are responsibilities for each role understood?
Roles and Hierarchy.guidance: Responsibilities for each role should be clearly understood by all SOC personnel

Roles and Hierarchy.question: Have you documented career progression requirements for each of these roles?
Roles and Hierarchy.guidance: Career progression for roles can be documented through training, certification, experience and soft skills requirements

Roles and Hierarchy.question: Do you regularly revise or update the role descriptions?
Roles and Hierarchy.guidance: To revise is to review and verify whether to documentation is still correct or requires an update

People Management.question: Do you have a job rotation plan in place?
People Management.guidance: Job rotation can be used to train employees in a variety of tasks and avoid too much routine

People Management.question: Do you have a career progression process in place?
Do you have a talent management process in place?
People Management.guidance: Talent should be adequately managed to retain such staff and fully develop their potential.

People Management.question: Do you have team diversity goals?
People Management.guidance: e.g. background diversity, ethnic diversity, gender diversity, etc.

People Management.question: Have you established team goals?
People Management.guidance: Team goals help to bring focus to the team and monitor progress

People Management.question: Do you document and track individual team member goals?
People Management.guidance: Individual team member goals should be set to help grow the employee to full potential

People Management.question: Do you periodically evaluate SOC employees?
People Management.guidance: Can also be included in the regular organization evaluation process

People Management.question: Do you have a 'new hire' process in place?
People Management.guidance: i.e. a defined process to quickly let new employees find their place and perform well in the SOC

People Management.question: Are all SOC employees subjected to screening?
People Management.guidance: Personnel screening is performed to avoid infiltration or misbehaviour by SOC employees

People Management.question: Do you measure employee satisfaction for improving the SOC?
People Management.guidance: Employee satisfaction should be taken seriously as lack of satisfaction may lead to key personnel leaving

People Management.question: Are there regular 1-on-1 meetings between the SOC manager and the employees?
People Management.guidance: Such informal 1-on-1 conversations are used to coach employees and help the SOC manager gain insight in personal challenges

People Management.question: Do you perform regular teambuilding exercises?
People Management.guidance: Teambuilding exercises are used to promote collaboration between individuals in the team and to raise team spirit

People Management.question: Do you perform regular teambuilding exercises with other teams relevant to the SOC?
People Management.guidance: In multi-team systems (MTS), the SOC collaborates with other teams. Use cross-team teambuilding to maximize performance

People Management.question: Do you periodically evaluate team performance?
People Management.guidance: Besides individual performance, team performance and dynamics are also important to measure and improve on

Knowledge Management.question: Do you have a formal knowledge management process in place?
Knowledge Management.guidance: Formal knowledge management helps to optimize knowledge creation and distribution

Knowledge Management.question: Do you have a skill matrix in place?
Knowledge Management.guidance: A matrix may consist of: SOC skills, SOC employees and skill levels (novice, intermediate, expert)

Knowledge Management.question: Please specify elements of the skill matrix:
Is the skill matrix actively used for team and personal improvement?
Knowledge Management.guidance: Personal improvement is essential, team improvement requires insight in team dynamics and skill distribution

Knowledge Management.question: Do you have a knowledge matrix in place?
Please specify elements of the knowledge matrix:
Is the knowledge matrix actively used to determine training and education needs?
Knowledge Management.guidance: The matrix should be used as a means to identify and resolve knowledge gaps

Knowledge Management.question: Have you documented SOC team member abilities?
Knowledge Management.guidance: Besides knowledge and skills, team member abilities are also important to document

Knowledge Management.question: Do you regularly assess and revise the knowledge management process?
Knowledge Management.guidance: This refers to the knowledge management process as a whole

Knowledge Management.question: Is there effective tooling in place to support knowledge documentation and distribution?
Knowledge Management.guidance: Such tooling can help to avoid investigation similar issues multiple times by integrating into the security monitoring process

Training and Education.question: Do you have a training program in place?
Training and Education.guidance: A training program is used to ensure a minimal level of knowledge for employees

Training and Education.question: Please specify elements of the training program:
Do you have a certification program in place?
Training and Education.guidance: A certification program is used to provide a demonstrable minimum level of knowledge and skills

Training and Education.question: Please specify elements of the certification program:
Is the training and certification program connected to evaluation and career progression?
Training and Education.guidance: e.g. certain training and certifications are required to grow from a junior level function to a more senior level function

Training and Education.question: Is there a reserved budget for education and training?
Training and Education.guidance: i.e. a fixed percentage of the total SOC budget that is allocated for education and cannot be used for other purposes

Training and Education.question: Is there a reserved amount of time for education and training?
Training and Education.guidance: This is an extension of education budget

Training and Education.question: Do you have regular workshops for knowledge development?
Training and Education.guidance: Workshops are an informal way of distributing knowledge

Training and Education.question: Do you regularly revise and update the training and certification programs?
Training and Education.guidance: Training and certification must be a relevant reflection of SOC knowledge and skill requirements

Management.question: Is there a SOC management process in place?
Management.guidance: A SOC management process is used to manage all aspects SOC service delivery and quality

Management.question: Are SOC management elements formally identified and documented?
Management.guidance: Possible SOC management elements can be found in under 1.3

Management.question: Please specify identified SOC management elements:
Is the SOC management process regularly reviewed?
Management.guidance: Regular review of the SOC management process ensures optimal performance

Management.question: Is the SOC management process aligned with all stakeholders?
Management.guidance: Alignment with stakeholders will ensure the SOC delivers services that meet customer expectations

Management.question: Have you implemented a process for continuous improvement (CI)?
Management.guidance: Continuous improvement is a vital process for SOCs to evolve their capabilities

Management.question: Specify elements of the continuous improvement program:
Have you implemented a process to manage SOC quality assurance (QA)?
Management.guidance: Quality assurance is aimed at ensuring SOC processes, technology and services meet their quality requirements

Management.question: Please specify elements of the quality assurance program:
Have you implemented a SOC architecture process?
Management.guidance: A SOC architecture describes how different components

Management.question: Please specify elements of the SOC architecture:

Operations and Facilities.question: Do you have a documented exercise plan?
Operations and Facilities.guidance: An exercise plan lists the type of exercises to be conducted, the frequency and the exercise goals

Operations and Facilities.question: Please specify types of exercises included in the plan
Do you perform security operations exercises regularly?
Operations and Facilities.guidance: Regularity should be matched to your own internal policy

Operations and Facilities.question: Are the results from exercises documented?
Operations and Facilities.guidance: Results from exercises should be structurally documented for future reference and identification of improvements

Operations and Facilities.question: Is the output from exercises actively used to improve security operations?
Operations and Facilities.guidance: Exercise output should be used to structurally improve security operations

Operations and Facilities.question: Do you have standard operating procedures?
Operations and Facilities.guidance: Standard operating procedures are used to provide consistent output

Operations and Facilities.question: Do you use checklists for recurring activities?
Operations and Facilities.guidance: Checklists can be useful to avoid recurring activities from being overlooked

Operations and Facilities.question: Do you use documented workflows?
Operations and Facilities.guidance: Workflows are used to standardize steps in, for example, security analysis

Operations and Facilities.question: Do you have a SOC operational handbook?
Operations and Facilities.guidance: A SOC operational handbook contains an overview of SOC tasks, as well as rules of engagement and expected behavior

Operations and Facilities.question: Have you established an Operational Security (OPSEC) program?
Operations and Facilities.guidance: An OPSEC program dictates security rules to ensure the integrity and confidentiality of SOC processes, tools and information

Operations and Facilities.question: Is the configuration management process integrated in the SOC?
Operations and Facilities.guidance: SOC services and procedures should be aligned and integrated with the organization's configuration management process

Operations and Facilities.question: Is the change management process integrated in the SOC?
Operations and Facilities.guidance: SOC services and procedures should be aligned and integrated with the organization's change management process

Operations and Facilities.question: Is the problem management process integrated in the SOC?
Operations and Facilities.guidance: SOC services and procedures should be aligned and integrated with the organization's problem management process

Operations and Facilities.question: Is the incident management process integrated in the SOC?
Operations and Facilities.guidance: SOC services and procedures should be aligned and integrated with the organization's incident management process

Operations and Facilities.question: Is the asset management process integrated in the SOC?
Operations and Facilities.guidance: SOC services and procedures should be aligned and integrated with the organization's asset management process

Operations and Facilities.question: Do you have a dedicated physical SOC location?
Operations and Facilities.guidance: A dedicated physical location decreases likelihood of unauthorized access and provides confidentiality for security incidents

Operations and Facilities.question: Do you have a war room for the SOC?
Operations and Facilities.guidance: A dedicated facility for coordination of major security incidents

Operations and Facilities.question: Do you have a dedicated network for the SOC?
Operations and Facilities.guidance: Given the confidentiality of the SOC and the importance of monitoring, it is recommended to use a separate network

Operations and Facilities.question: Do you have physical access control to the SOC location?
Operations and Facilities.guidance: e.g. key cards (badges) for access with access logging

Operations and Facilities.question: Do you have a secure physical storage location?
Operations and Facilities.guidance: Secure storage facilities can be used to store evidence collected during investigations or other operational security purposes

Operations and Facilities.question: Do you have a video wall for monitoring purposes?
Operations and Facilities.guidance: A video wall can be used to display the real-time security status and can be used for decision making as well as PR

Operations and Facilities.question: Do you have a call-center capability for the SOC?
Operations and Facilities.guidance: Since communication and coordination are important features of a SOC, call-center capability may be required

Operations and Facilities.question: Do you have specialized analyst workstations?
Operations and Facilities.guidance: e.g. multiple screen setup, virtual machines, etc.

Operations and Facilities.question: Have you optimized secure remote working capabilities for SOC employees?
Operations and Facilities.guidance: Secure working enabled means secure access (MFA, encryption, etc.), secure working facilitated also means equipped and performing

Operations and Facilities.question: Do you use shift schedules?
Operations and Facilities.guidance: Shift schedules are used to ensure full shift coverage

Operations and Facilities.question: Have schedules been created to optimize vigilance during shifts?
Operations and Facilities.guidance: Schedules should be created to optimize vigilance. Thus, shift should include mandatory breaks and not be too long

Operations and Facilities.question: Do you have a shift log?
Operations and Facilities.guidance: A shift log covers all exceptions found during the shift, running investigations, etc.

Operations and Facilities.question: Do you have a formally described shift turnover procedure?
Operations and Facilities.guidance: i.e. a procedure for handing over a shift and exchanging information regarding running tasks or issues for further follow-up

Operations and Facilities.question: Do you have a daily SOC operational stand-up?
Operations and Facilities.guidance: This can also be a call in case physical attendance is not possible for all attendees

Operations and Facilities.question: Do you have stand-by arrangements with employees within the SOC?
Operations and Facilities.guidance: i.e. is there a formal stand-by function that obligates employees to be able to be reached within a certain time?

Operations and Facilities.question: Do you have a Document Management System in place?
Operations and Facilities.guidance: The system should support different file types, authorizations and version management; possibly even encryption

Operations and Facilities.question: Do you have a knowledge & collaboration platform in place?
Operations and Facilities.guidance: e.g. a wiki space or SharePoint that allows collaboration and supports team efforts

Reporting & communication.question: Do you regularly provide reports?
Reporting & communication.guidance: Regular reports help to keep customers informed of SOC activities

Reporting & communication.question: Are these reports tailored to the recipients?
Reporting & communication.guidance: e.g. management reports for senior management, technical reports for the IT organization

Reporting & communication.question: Are the report contents approved by or reviewed by the recipients?
Reporting & communication.guidance: formal sign-off can be part of a larger service delivery sign-off

Reporting & communication.question: Do you have established reporting lines within the organization?
Reporting & communication.guidance: e.g. reporting lines could be: SOC management, IT management, senior management

Reporting & communication.question: Do you regularly revise and update the report templates?
Reporting & communication.guidance: Report templates should be regularly optimized to ensure continued

Reporting & communication.question: Do you have formal agreements with the recipients regarding reports?
Reporting & communication.guidance: For example: timelines of delivery, report contents, etc.

Reporting & communication.question: Do you provide different types of reports to your recipients?
Reporting & communication.guidance: Different types of reports provide more insight into security operations

Reporting & communication.question: Do you use different types of metrics in your reports?
Reporting & communication.guidance: Different types of metrics provide more insight into security operations

Reporting & communication.question: Do you provide advisories to the organization regarding threats and vulnerabilities?
Reporting & communication.guidance: Advisories are used to inform customers of security threats and vulnerabilities

Reporting & communication.question: Do you perform risk / impact assessments of these advisories?
Reporting & communication.guidance: i.e. do you add organizational context to these advisories?

Reporting & communication.question: Do you perform follow-up of these advisories?
Reporting & communication.guidance: i.e. do you assist in coordination when required?

Reporting & communication.question: Do you provide education and security awareness to the organization?
Reporting & communication.guidance: The SOC may be involved in security awareness and education to make users in the organisation aware of their role in cyber security

Reporting & communication.question: Do you measure the effect of education and security awareness efforts?
Reporting & communication.guidance: Measuring the efforts is necessary for improvement of the security awareness function

Reporting & communication.question: Do you use communication templates?
Reporting & communication.guidance: Communication templates help to standardize and professionalize SOC communication to stakeholders

Reporting & communication.question: Do you have a communication matrix in place?
Reporting & communication.guidance: A communication matrix can be used to decide when, how and with whom to communicate

Reporting & communication.question: Is communication training (verbal/written) available for SOC personnel?
Reporting & communication.guidance: Communication training helps SOC personnel to communicate effectively

Reporting & communication.question: Are communication skills element of SOC role descriptions?
Reporting & communication.guidance: Communication skills are important for analysts to explain their findings and recommendations

Use Case Management.question: Is there a use case management process or framework in place?
Use Case Management.guidance: A framework, such as MaGMa UCF, can be used to guide use case lifecycle and document use case in a standardized format

Use Case Management.question: Are use cases formally documented?
Use Case Management.guidance: Formal documentation may include use case documentation templates

Use Case Management.question: Are use cases approved by relevant stakeholders?
Use Case Management.guidance: e.g. business stakeholders, IT stakeholders, CISOs, audit & compliance, risk management, etc.

Use Case Management.question: Is the use case management process aligned with other important processes?
Use Case Management.guidance: e.g. integration with the threat / risk management process to revise use cases when the threat landscape changes

Use Case Management.question: Are use cases created using a standardized process?
Use Case Management.guidance: i.e. a standardized approach to derive use cases from threats or business requirements

Use Case Management.question: Are use cases created using a top-down approach?
Use Case Management.guidance: e.g. use cases can be derived from business requirements, risk assessments, threat management / intelligence

Use Case Management.question: Can use cases be traced from high-level drivers to low-level implementation?
Use Case Management.guidance: Top-down traceability is important to determine completeness of implementation and demonstrable risk reduction

Use Case Management.question: Can use cases be traced from low-level implementation to high-level drivers?
Use Case Management.guidance: Bottom-up traceability is important for contextualizing use case output and business alignment

Use Case Management.question: Are use cases measured for implementation and effectiveness?
Use Case Management.guidance: Metrics can be applied to use cases to determine growth and maturity by measuring effectiveness and implementation

Use Case Management.question: Are use cases scored and prioritized based on risk levels?
Use Case Management.guidance: Risks can be (cyber)threats, but also non-compliance or penalties (laws & regulations)

Use Case Management.question: Are use cases regularly revised and updated?
Use Case Management.guidance: Use cases should be subjected to life cycle management and may require updates or may be outdated and decommissioned

Use Case Management.question: Do you measure use cases against the MITRE ATT&CK® framework for gap analysis purposes?
Use Case Management.guidance: By measuring use cases against MITRE ATT&CK®, it is possible to determine strengths and weaknesses in your layered detection approach

Use Case Management.question: Are monitoring rules tagged with MITRE ATT&CK® framework identifiers?
Use Case Management.guidance: Tagging monitoring rules with MITRE ATT&CK® identifiers allows for reporting on sightings of attack techniques

Use Case Management.question: Have you created a MITRE ATT&CK® risk profile for your organization?
Use Case Management.guidance: The creation of a risk profile in MITRE ATT&CK® can help to identify relevant attack techniques

Use Case Management.question: Have you prioritized MITRE ATT&CK® techniques for relevance?
Use Case Management.guidance: Using organizational context (protection and detection mechanisms), ATT&CK® techniques can be prioritized

Use Case Management.question: Is use case output (alerts) used in threat intelligence activities?
Use Case Management.guidance: Using MITRE ATT&CK®, it is possible to connect alerts to specific threat actors, or potentially even active campaigns

Use Case Management.question: Is threat intelligence used for the creation and updates of use cases?
Use Case Management.guidance: Threat intelligence can provide input into security monitoring, especially when using MITRE ATT&CK® to connect both

Use Case Management.question: Do you determine and document visibility requirements for each use case?
Use Case Management.guidance: Data source requirements should be part of use case design

Use Case Management.question: Do you measure visibility status for your use cases for gap analysis purposes?
Use Case Management.guidance: Measuring visibility status of use cases will help to identify use cases that require additional data sources for detection optimization

Use Case Management.question: Do you map data source visibility to the MITRE ATT&CK® framework?
Use Case Management.guidance: Mapping available data sources to MITRE ATT&CK® data source requirements will help identify gaps in visibility of attack techniques

Detection Engineering & Validation.question: Do you have a detection engineering process in place?
Detection Engineering & Validation.guidance: A detection engineering process supports the creation and deployment of detection rules for security monitoring purposes

Detection Engineering & Validation.question: Is the detection engineering process formally documented?
Detection Engineering & Validation.guidance: Formal documentation supports process standardisation, and allows for faster training of new engineers

Detection Engineering & Validation.question: Are there specific roles and requirements for detection engineers?
Detection Engineering & Validation.guidance: Detection engineers have a skillset that is different from security analysts and security engineers

Detection Engineering & Validation.question: Is there active cooperation between the SOC analysts and the detection engineers?
Detection Engineering & Validation.guidance: SOC analyst deal with alerts resulting from detections created by engineers, so a tight interaction is required to optimize the ruleset

Detection Engineering & Validation.question: Is there active cooperation between the Threat Intelligence analysts and detection engineers?
Detection Engineering & Validation.guidance: Threat intelligence is a major input into the creation or updating of detection rules

Detection Engineering & Validation.question: Are there formal hand-over to the analyst team?
Detection Engineering & Validation.guidance: Once the detections are created, they must be operationalized. This should be done with a formal hand-over to production

Detection Engineering & Validation.question: Is there a testing enviroment to test and validate detections before deploying them?
Detection Engineering & Validation.guidance: A testing environment allows for thorough testing of new detections, which ensures a higher level of quality

Detection Engineering & Validation.question: Is there a formal release process in place for new detections?
Detection Engineering & Validation.guidance: A formal release process includes automated deployment of rules and adheres to organizational change management procedures

Detection Engineering & Validation.question: Do you apply a versioning system to detections?
Detection Engineering & Validation.guidance: A versioning system will allow to revert back to previous versions of detections

Detection Engineering & Validation.question: Do you have a roll-back procedure in place in case of problems with detections?
Detection Engineering & Validation.guidance: A roll-back procedure enabled reverting back to a good state if a deployment has an adverse effect on security monitoring

Detection Engineering & Validation.question: Do you perform adversary emulation or automated detection testing?
Detection Engineering & Validation.guidance: These validation activities provides insights into how well security monitoring is able to detect certain adversaries or attack techniques

Detection Engineering & Validation.question: Do you test for detection of MITRE ATT&CK® techniques?
Detection Engineering & Validation.guidance: Testing for MITRE ATT&CK® techniques can augment mapping of use cases and visibility in Mitre ATT&CK

Detection Engineering & Validation.question: Do you test detection analytics not directly associated with MITRE ATT&CK®?
Detection Engineering & Validation.guidance: Not all use cases and risks have a relationship to MITRE ATT&CK®. These use cases should be tested as well

Detection Engineering & Validation.question: Do you test response playbooks?
Detection Engineering & Validation.guidance: Testing both detection and response provides a more complete view of SOC capabilities

Detection Engineering & Validation.question: Is detection validation fully integrated in the detection engineering process / pipeline?
Detection Engineering & Validation.guidance: When deploying new or updated detection, automated detection testing should be executed as a quality gate

Detection Engineering & Validation.question: Is the outcome from detection validation used as input into monitoring and detection engineering?
Detection Engineering & Validation.guidance: Output should lead to updates in detections and new detections, as well as instructions for SOC analysts

Detection Engineering & Validation.question: Do you monitor the data ingestion status for data sources?
Detection Engineering & Validation.guidance: Monitoring data ingestion is used to identify data ingestion problems or inactive data sources

Detection Engineering & Validation.question: Do you actively measure and improve data source coverage?
Detection Engineering & Validation.guidance: Data source coverage should be optimized to avoid blind spots in monitoring

Maturity.guidance: Contractual agreements should also cover penalties

Maturity.question: Is sufficient personnel allocated to the process to ensure required service delivery?
Maturity.guidance: Allocation of dedicated personnel will ensure highest service quality

Maturity.question: Is the service aligned with other relevant processes?
Maturity.guidance: e.g. the security monitoring process, and mainly the security incident management process

Maturity.question: Is there a incident resolution / service continuity process in place for this service?
Maturity.guidance: Service continuity is important to comply with contractual agreements, even in case of major incidents

Maturity.question: Has a set of procedures been created for this service?
Maturity.guidance: Procedures support process standardization and quality. Personnel should be trained to use procedures correctly and structurally

Maturity.question: Is there an onboarding and offloading procedure for this service?
Maturity.guidance: Customer onboarding and offloading procedures support efficient service delivery and ensure customers are (dis)connected properly

Maturity.question: Are best practices applied to the service?
Maturity.guidance: Best practices should be used to optimize this service

Maturity.question: Is process data gathered for prediction of service performance?
Maturity.guidance: Service performance measurement requires establishment of performance goals

Maturity.question: Is the service continuously being improved based on improvement goals?
Maturity.guidance: Improvement based on based evaluation, (maturity) assessment, tests, etc.
